newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos declares a state of calamity in at least eight towns in southern Mindanao island ravaged by two weeks of fighting between the army and Moslem rebels. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Defence Secretary Renato de Villa belittles the threat of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front to pull out from peace talks and launch an all-out war unless the military offensive against rebel forces is stopped (MANILA STANDARD)

- Hotel operators and local government officials in Boracay island urge the Department of Environment and Natural Resources to retract its warning that the island's waters are unsafe for swimming. (ALL PAPERS)
- The local manufacturing industry rebounds as the volume of production index grows by 9.3 percent in April from a 0.6 percent growth in March (ALL PAPERS)
- Shareholders of Australian softdrink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd approve an agreement with San Miguel Corp to create the largest Coca-Cola bottler outside the United States. (TODAY)
- The outstanding public debt in the first quarter of the year reaches 1.322 trillion pesos from 1.331 trillion as of end-December 1996 (ALL PAPERS)
- Net foreign investments, both direct and portoflio, contracted to $238 million in the first quarter of the year, the Central Bank says. (BUSINESSWORLD)
